correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\ge1\), a uniform-root decomposition gives \(K_n=n^{-1}\sum_{j<n}K_j+g_n\). Conditional mean path length is \(c_j+c_{n-1-j}\), while conditional maximum-search visits average \(H_j\). The explicit weighted-harmonic-square and harmonic-convolution identities in the proof yield \(g_n=(n+1)(3/2-H_n^{(2)})-H_n/n\); telescoping gives \(K_n=3n+H_n-2(n+1)H_n^{(2)}\). Opposite reflected monotonicities of the discrete-convex path-length mean and symmetrized harmonic mean establish \(g_n<0\) for every \(n\ge3\), and recurrence preserves strict negativity. Harmonic expansions, independent record indicators, and the cited Quicksort variance give the correlation asymptotic. Exact-rational enumeration through eight keys, root-split checks through 120 keys and large-size numeric illustrations passed, but these finite checks do not replace the proof for all sizes. Correlation is defined only where both variances are positive, namely \(n\ge3\).

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The mixed covariance is not determined by separate first and second moments of P or R, nor by covariance of P with a symmetric root-imbalance parameter, a leaf count, or a deterministic tree-size statistic. originality.rationale: The exact mixed covariance \(3n+H_n-2(n+1)H_n^{(2)}\), the strict all-size negative sign, and the asymptotic correlation coefficient are not stated in the inspected primary texts. Classical marginal BST/Quicksort moments, permutation-record distributions, record-biased trees, label-weighted depths, and path-length/space-requirement covariances do not alone imply this joint law. An older implicit generating function could still cover it; this remains a material historical risk.
residual_risks: A classical but unlocated joint generating function for first-pivot Quicksort comparisons and permutation upper records might imply the exact covariance.

Differentiating an unpublished or less visible expected total path length under a record-biased permutation law at unit bias would recover the covariance; the inspected record-biased articles do not supply this expectation.
The older paper on random records/cuttings in BSTs was inspected only at abstract level; its described random-cut records differ from insertion-permutation upper records.
Older books and specialized joint-cost articles were not exhaustively inspected; the outcome is a self-review, not an independent historical-priority certification.

value.rationale: Two natural and genuinely different costs of the same random search tree—a global sum over all node depths and the extreme-key successful-search path—have a complete exact negative covariance law not inferable from the known marginal moments. The root-split convexity mechanism explains the sign, the exact closed form characterizes every sample size, and the asymptotic reveals linear covariance with Pearson correlation approaching zero. This structural dependence is motivated by interpreting insertion/search performance jointly, rather than by a fabricated or arbitrary parameter slice.
